summary: The article argues that the heavy media coverage of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's romance, though irritating to hardcore fans, may be a strategic business boost for the NFL as it chases Roger Goodell's $27 billion revenue target for 2027. It cites jersey sales, viewership and fan-base figures, then compares the NFL's image problems with the NBA's 1970s decline and recovery under David Stern.
one_line: The Swift-Kelce coverage may be savvy business for the NFL's push toward $27 billion and global reach, echoing the NBA's recovery under David Stern.
key_facts: Reality TV star Rachel Lindsay, a longtime NFL fan, slammed the "obnoxious" Swift-Kelce coverage and called the uptick in Swifties obsessing over football "exhausting".
The NFL began in 1920 and is now an $18 billion league; Commissioner Roger Goodell has set a $27 billion target for 2027.
Taylor Swift is a 12-time Grammy winner with 103.7992 million Swifties, compared with 184 million football fans; the article estimates adding about 104 million fans could lift revenue to $28 billion.
TMZ reported that Travis Kelce's #87 jersey sales rose 400% and his Instagram followers rose 276%.
Yahoo Finance reported a 53% rise in viewership among teen girls.
The October 1 Chiefs vs. Jets game drew 27 million viewers, the most-watched Sunday TV show since the last Super Bowl, which featured a Rihanna concert.
The NFL has scheduled 5 games abroad this season and introduced new concussion rules plus a $100 million initiative called "Play Smart, Play Safe".
Joe Pompliano said the NFL will bring in $20 billion this year, more than the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A and Ligue 1 combined.
The English Premier League is broadcast in over 212 territories but has revenue of just $6 billion.
In the 1970s the NBA averaged around 8,000 attendance per game and faced drug abuse and brawls; the Washington Post reported estimates of player cocaine use from 40 percent to 75 percent.
Commissioner David Stern instituted an anti-drug agreement, banned All-Star Michael Richardson for life, and opened Olympic basketball to NBA players, producing the 1992 "Dream Team".
The US has never failed to win a medal in the 19 Olympic basketball games played since 1992.

NFL controversies include Colin Kaepernick's kneeling, domestic violence cases, Deflategate, Bountygate, and the Union of Concerned Scientists' accusation that the NFL tried to intimidate scientists studying CTE.
